candidate-models.t: Five candidates for the eight development houses: **a straight line** and a **degree-4 curve** with ridge strength **λ = 0, 0.1, 0.3 and 1**. Which one will predict new houses best?

train.t: Each candidate is fitted to the development data. The flexible curve with **λ = 0 hugs the points** tightly; a stronger λ smooths it out.

validation.t: Four-fold cross-validation scores each candidate on houses it was **not trained on**: line **0.0359**, curve λ = 0 **0.3169**, λ = 0.1 **0.2769**, λ = 0.3 **0.1662**, λ = 1 **0.4682**.

compare-metrics.t: Training error and validation error tell **different stories**. The λ = 0 curve has the smallest training error but a validation error almost **nine times** the line's.

reject-overfit.t: A **tiny training error with a large validation error** is the signature of overfitting. Ridge helps the curve (λ = 0.3 is its best) but not enough.

select.t: The straight line has the **lowest validation error**, so it wins. A simpler model beats a fancier one when the data are close to a line.

lock-choice.t: Refit the winner on **all development houses** and freeze every decision: the model, its hyperparameters, everything. From now on **nothing may change in response to the test set**.

final-test.t: Only now do we score the two locked test houses: **test MSE 0.0046**, in the same small range as the validation scores. If it were disappointing we would **report it, not go back and tune**.

workflow-summary.t: **Train** to learn parameters, **validate or cross-validate** to choose the model and hyperparameters, **lock** the choice, **test once** to report. This is how we avoid fooling ourselves.
